source: NCERT Class XI, Indian Constitution at Work, Ch. 4 (Executive).

sections.heading: 1. Parliamentary Executive in India
points: The **executive** implements laws and runs the administration.
India has a **parliamentary system** (from Britain): the **real executive** (PM + Council of Ministers) is **responsible to the legislature (Lok Sabha)**.
The **President** is the **nominal/constitutional head** (head of state), while the **Prime Minister** is the head of government (real power).

sections.heading: 2. The President
points: Elected **indirectly** by an **electoral college** (elected MPs + elected MLAs) using **proportional representation (STV)**; term **5 years**.
Powers: executive (appointments), legislative (assent to bills, ordinances Art 123), judicial (pardons Art 72), emergency (National — Art 352, President's Rule — Art 356, Financial — Art 360).
The President acts on the **aid and advice of the Council of Ministers (Art 74)** — advice is **binding** (42nd/44th Amendments).

sections.heading: 3. Prime Minister and Council of Ministers
points: The **PM** is appointed by the President (leader of the majority party in Lok Sabha); the PM heads the Council of Ministers.
**Collective responsibility** — the Council is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha (falls if it loses confidence).
Ministers: Cabinet Ministers, Ministers of State, Deputy Ministers.
The PM is the **most powerful functionary** — links the President, Cabinet and Parliament.

sections.heading: 4. Permanent Executive — Bureaucracy
points: The **civil services (bureaucracy)** = the **permanent executive**, which implements policies (unlike the political executive that changes).
**All India Services (IAS, IPS, IFoS)**, Central and State services; recruited by the **UPSC/State PSCs**.
The bureaucracy is meant to be **politically neutral, professional and accountable**.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: India = parliamentary executive; PM = real head, President = nominal head.
President elected indirectly (electoral college, STV); term 5 years.
Art 74 = President acts on binding advice of Council of Ministers.
Collective responsibility of Council to the Lok Sabha.
Bureaucracy = permanent executive; recruited via UPSC (politically neutral).

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: The **President is the nominal head**; the **PM is the real executive**.
The President is **elected indirectly** (by an electoral college), not by direct vote.
Under **Art 74** the President must act on the **binding advice** of the Council of Ministers.
The **Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha** (not Rajya Sabha).
